proof_of_reserves.bitquery_address_label_claim: All 17 drained wallets carry Binance proof-of-reserves labels in Bitquery's address data; this includes its five XRPL source accounts.
proof_of_reserves.coin_desk_crosswalk_scope: Binance 14 Ethereum wallet identified in October 1 PoR; not the five XRPL accounts.
proof_of_reserves.expected_publication_window: By 2026-11-07 under Binance's published monthly reporting schedule

incident_cause.binance_initial_hypothesis: Compromised DevOps engineer computer/laptop gave access to an internal service.
incident_cause.later_binance_statement: Additional breach points were found; the computer may have been the entry point; fuller report pending.
incident_cause.trm_assessment_as_reported_by_reuters: Transaction-signing infrastructure was compromised and authorized withdrawals.
incident_cause.private_key_exfiltration: NOT_ESTABLISHED; Binance said no evidence of wallet private-key leakage.

evidence_classification.confirmed_on_chain: Five previously reconciled XRPL payments total 233,461,943.1 XRP; the receiver and transaction IDs are recorded in earlier immutable snapshots.
evidence_classification.sourced_claim: Bitquery labels all 17 drained hot wallets as Binance PoR addresses and reports the five XRPL accounts within that set.
evidence_classification.corroboration: Reuters independently reports the revised signing-infrastructure assessment and Binance's USD 6.34B coverage commitment; CoinDesk separately reconciles Binance 14 to the October 1 Ethereum PoR snapshot.
evidence_classification.inference: The XRP source accounts likely belonged to the PoR-labelled wallet universe, but official file-level membership is not yet verified.
evidence_classification.unknown: Post-06:43 XRP receiver balance; exact five-wallet match to Binance's official downloadable October 1 address file; post-incident XRP reserve ratio; exact token-level replenishment; exact signing-service attack path.
evidence_classification.disconfirming_or_qualifying: The XRP/Solana receivers share no address with other chain clusters; Bitquery links the XRP leg to the incident through timing, transaction construction and Binance's aggregate loss. Binance's USD 6.34B commitment may offset customer shortfalls, but does not prove the original XRP wallets have been replenished.

hypotheses.claim: The five XRPL sending accounts were part of Binance's proof-of-reserves wallet universe.
hypotheses.disconfirming_evidence: Bitquery's provider labels are not a direct official Binance address-file match; CoinDesk's published crosswalk in the reviewed article concerns Binance 14 on Ethereum.

hypotheses.claim: The attacker gained the ability to induce Binance's transaction-signing infrastructure to authorize withdrawals across chains.
hypotheses.disconfirming_evidence: Binance has not published the complete postmortem or exact authorization path; no wallet private-key leakage has been established.

hypotheses.claim: Binance's announced USD 6.34B in company resources may restore affected customer balances and replace stolen tokens.
hypotheses.disconfirming_evidence: The aggregate company statement does not disclose XRP-specific purchases, wallet replenishment, current reserve ratio or completed customer-level reconciliation.

hypotheses.claim: The 233.5M XRP held by the attacker may become future sell-side supply if moved into liquid venues.
hypotheses.disconfirming_evidence: No sale or exchange deposit was identified by Bitquery's 06:43 UTC cutoff; later disposition is unknown and Binance has committed to cover customer losses.

market_feature_admission.reason: The XRP balance cutoff is 06:43 UTC, market panels are asynchronous, and reserve membership/replenishment remain incomplete. The event is retained as a timestamped research covariate candidate, not a live directional signal.
